translation: A stranger came to the inn. He was hungry, and he was sick. One of the monks saw the stranger. The monk gave him food and water. The stranger said, “You do not deny me food.” The monk said, “I feed you with good food.” The stranger ate the food and drank the water.
nominal_check: The cuman token is an accusative object in the narrative; cuma tokens are nominative subjects. Munuca is partitive genitive plural. Mętes is genitive in denial; gōde męte is instrumental means. Mē in the stranger’s speech and ðē in the monk’s speech both refer to the stranger; their speaker/addressee roles differ.
